spec.description: The City of Melbourne's street sensors: some 6,300 parking bays as they are now, about 100 pedestrian counters hour by hour, and the microclimate stations' temperature, noise and particles; reloaded every 5 minutes.

options.content:
### Where the data comes from

The City of Melbourne publishes what its sensors measure as open data, on [its portal](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/), with no key. This dashboard reads three of its networks, in the city centre and around it:

- **[On-street parking bay sensors](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/on-street-parking-bay-sensors/)**: a sensor in the road surface under each of some 6,300 bays says whether a car is over it. The portal holds each bay's latest state and when it last changed, refreshed every few minutes. The streets come from the [bays' register](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/on-street-parking-bays/) and, failing that, from the [bay's parking zone](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/parking-zones-linked-to-street-segments/).
- **[Pedestrian counting system](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/pedestrian-counting-system-monthly-counts-per-hour/)**: about 100 counters (laser and thermal sensors on poles and awnings) count the people walking past each way, hour by hour, around the clock since 2009. The counts are loaded once a day, so the latest hours are a day or two old.
- **[Microclimate sensors](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/microclimate-sensors-data/)**: a dozen stations on poles and rooftops measure temperature, humidity, wind, fine particles and noise about every 15 minutes. Only some still report: those silent in the time range do not show.

### How to read it

- A bay's state is now; the time range does not change it. A sensor that has not changed in a week is shown grey and left out of the counts: in the city centre a bay is not taken, or free, that long, so the sensor is taken as broken or switched off. A bay with no sensor does not show at all.
- The pedestrian counts are the time range's, up to its last 31 days; the microclimate readings, up to its last 14.
- Noise is in decibels (dB): 55 dB is a quiet street, 70 dB a busy one with traffic.

### How it works

Grafana's DuckDB reads the three datasets through the stack's gateway, which keeps each a while (the bays and the microclimate two minutes, the counts an hour), so the portal is asked once whoever is looking. DuckDB running in your browser (the Chaski data source) then answers every panel and every click. The map is the Kepler Geospatial Maps Plus panel, with its Sparkline layer. The dashboard reloads every five minutes.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT time, coalesce(way_1, 'One way') AS way, dir_1 AS people FROM $peds WHERE sensor = $sensor
UNION ALL
SELECT time, coalesce(way_2, 'The other way') AS way, dir_2 AS people FROM $peds WHERE sensor = $sensor
ORDER BY time

spec.description: The counter clicked on the map, its hourly count each way past it. Click another to change it.
spec.title: The counter picked on the map

spec.rawSql:
WITH last AS (WITH days AS (SELECT day, count(DISTINCT hour) AS hours FROM $peds GROUP BY day)
SELECT max(day) AS day FROM days WHERE hours = 24),
full_days AS (SELECT day FROM $peds GROUP BY day HAVING count(DISTINCT hour) = 24)
SELECT name AS "Counter",
       sum(people) FILTER (WHERE day = (SELECT day FROM last))::BIGINT AS "Latest full day",
       (sum(people) FILTER (WHERE day IN (SELECT day FROM full_days))
          / nullif(count(DISTINCT day) FILTER (WHERE day IN (SELECT day FROM full_days)), 0))::BIGINT AS "Mean day",
       max(people) AS "Busiest hour",
       arg_max(time, people) AS "When"
FROM $peds
GROUP BY name
ORDER BY "Latest full day" DESC NULLS LAST

spec.description: Every counter: people past it on the latest full day, its mean day over the full days of the time range, and its busiest hour in the range.
spec.title: Pedestrian counters, busiest first

spec.rawSql:
WITH last AS (WITH days AS (SELECT day, count(DISTINCT hour) AS hours FROM $peds GROUP BY day)
SELECT max(day) AS day FROM days WHERE hours = 24)
SELECT sum(people)::BIGINT AS "People" FROM $peds, last WHERE $peds.day = last.day

spec.description: People counted past every counter on the latest day all 24 hours of which are in, in Melbourne's time. The city loads the counts once a day, so that day is a day or two ago. A person passing two counters counts twice.
spec.title: Pedestrians, latest full day

spec.rawSql:
WITH last AS (WITH days AS (SELECT day, count(DISTINCT hour) AS hours FROM $peds GROUP BY day)
SELECT max(day) AS day FROM days WHERE hours = 24)
SELECT strftime(strptime(day, '%Y-%m-%d'), '%a %d %b') AS "Day" FROM last

spec.description: The latest day with all 24 hours of counts in.
spec.title: That day

spec.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Free') AS "Free" FROM $bays

spec.description: Bays whose sensor says free, of those that have changed in the last week.
spec.title: Bays free now

spec.rawSql:
-- Every bay, coloured by what its sensor says now.
SELECT bay, zone, street, segment, status, since, latitude, longitude FROM $bays

-- Every counter, hour by hour, for the cards.
SELECT sensor, name, latitude, longitude, time, people FROM $peds ORDER BY sensor, time

-- The last day of readings, one row each: the time filter picks the moment, and
-- the Measure picker the column drawn as "value" (Chaski quotes a variable's
-- value; :raw gives the bare column name). A day, not the whole range: the colour
-- scale spans the rows it gets, and a week of temperatures (5 to 28 °C) would
-- paint the degree or two between stations at one moment in a single band. A
-- station that lacks the measure (Royal Park has no noise or particles) drops out.
SELECT station, place, time, temperature, humidity, wind, noise, pm25,
       ${metric:raw} AS value,
       printf('%.1f', ${metric:raw})
         || CASE ${metric} WHEN 'temperature' THEN ' °C' WHEN 'humidity' THEN ' %' WHEN 'noise' THEN ' dB'
                           WHEN 'pm25' THEN ' µg/m³' ELSE '' END AS reading,
       latitude, longitude
FROM $climate
WHERE ${metric:raw} IS NOT NULL AND time > (SELECT max(time) FROM $climate) - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
ORDER BY station, time

spec.description: Every parking bay with a sensor, as it is now: blue is free, orange is taken, and grey is a sensor that has not changed in a week, taken as gone quiet. The bigger dots are the pedestrian counters: hover one for its hourly counts over the time range, all on one scale, and its colour is its latest hour. The white dots are the microclimate stations, with their latest temperature and street noise. Click a counter to see it below.
spec.title: Parking bays, pedestrians and microclimate

spec.rawSql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT station, max(time) AS t, arg_max(noise, time) AS v FROM $climate
                WHERE noise IS NOT NULL GROUP BY station)
SELECT median(v) AS "Noise" FROM latest WHERE t > (SELECT max(t) FROM latest) - INTERVAL 1 HOUR

spec.description: The median of the latest noise readings, in decibels, of the stations that measure it and reported in the last hour. 55 dB is a quiet street, 70 dB a busy one.
spec.title: Street noise now

spec.rawSql:
SELECT 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Occupied') / nullif(count(*), 0) AS "Occupancy"
FROM $bays WHERE status <> 'Silent for a week'

spec.description: Occupied bays as a share of the bays reporting: free and occupied, not the silent ones.
spec.title: Occupancy

spec.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Occupied') AS "Occupied" FROM $bays

spec.description: Bays whose sensor says a car is there, of those that have changed in the last week.
spec.title: Bays occupied now

spec.rawSql: SELECT time, sum(people)::BIGINT AS people FROM $peds GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

spec.description: People counted in each hour past all the counters together. The city loads a day's counts once a day, so the line stops a day or two before now.
spec.title: Pedestrians by the hour, every counter

spec.rawSql: SELECT time, place, pm25 FROM $climate WHERE pm25 IS NOT NULL ORDER BY time

spec.description: Each station's PM2.5, in µg/m³, from low-cost sensors: good for when it rises, less so for how much. The WHO's guideline for a 24-hour mean is 15 µg/m³.
spec.title: Fine particles (PM2.5)

spec.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Silent for a week') AS "Silent" FROM $bays

spec.description: Bay sensors that have not changed in a week: a bay in the city centre does not stay taken, or free, that long, so these are taken as broken or switched off.
spec.title: Sensors silent

spec.rawSql: SELECT time, place, noise FROM $climate WHERE noise IS NOT NULL ORDER BY time

spec.description: Each station's noise level, in decibels. The Royal Park weather station does not measure it.
spec.title: Street noise

spec.rawSql:
SELECT street AS "Street",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Occupied') AS "Taken",
       100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Occupied') / count(*) AS "Occupancy"
FROM $bays WHERE status <> 'Silent for a week' AND street <> 'Unknown'
GROUP BY street HAVING count(*) >= 10
ORDER BY "Occupancy" DESC

spec.description: Every street with at least ten bays reporting, by the share of them taken now: how many are taken, and what share of those reporting. Silent sensors are left out.
spec.title: Streets, fullest first

spec.rawSql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT station, max(time) AS t, arg_max(temperature, time) AS v FROM $climate GROUP BY station)
SELECT median(v) AS "Temperature" FROM latest WHERE t > (SELECT max(t) FROM latest) - INTERVAL 1 HOUR

spec.description: The median of the microclimate stations' latest readings, of those that reported in the last hour.
spec.title: Air temperature now

spec.rawSql: SELECT time, place, temperature FROM $climate WHERE temperature IS NOT NULL ORDER BY time

spec.description: Each microclimate station's air temperature, reading by reading, about every 15 minutes.
spec.title: Air temperature
Melbourne street sensors: parking, pedestrians and microclimate

spec.description: The microclimate measure the stations and the surface draw.
spec.label: Measure
spec.name: metric
spec.query: Temperature (°C) : temperature,Humidity (%) : humidity,Wind speed : wind,Street noise (dB) : noise,Fine particles PM2.5 (µg/m³) : pm25

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: every parking bay sensor the City of Melbourne runs, and what
-- it says now, through the gateway, which keeps the list two minutes (see
-- gateway/feeds.conf). Each bay's street comes from the bays' register, by
-- kerbside id. The timestamp is when the bay last changed: a bay that has not
-- changed in a week is taken as a sensor gone quiet, not a car parked for it.
WITH sensors AS (
  SELECT kerbsideid, zone_number, status_description, status_timestamp,
         ST_Y(location) AS latitude, ST_X(location) AS longitude
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/on-street-parking-bay-sensors.parquet')
),
streets AS (
  SELECT TRY_CAST(kerbsideid AS BIGINT) AS kerbsideid, any_value(roadsegmentdescription) AS segment
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/on-street-parking-bays.parquet?select=kerbsideid,roadsegmentdescription&where=kerbsideid%20is%20not%20null')
  GROUP BY 1
),
zones AS (
  SELECT parkingzone AS zone_number, any_value(onstreet) AS onstreet,
         any_value(onstreet || ' between ' || streetfrom || ' and ' || streetto) AS zsegment
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/parking-zones-linked-to-street-segments.parquet')
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT s.kerbsideid::VARCHAR                                  AS bay,
       s.zone_number                                         AS zone,
       coalesce(t.segment, z.zsegment, 'Unknown')            AS segment,
       coalesce(nullif(regexp_extract(t.segment, '^(.*?) between ', 1), ''), t.segment, z.onstreet, 'Unknown') AS street,
       CASE WHEN s.status_timestamp < now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY THEN 'Silent for a week'
            WHEN s.status_description = 'Present'           THEN 'Occupied'
            ELSE 'Free' END                                  AS status,
       s.status_timestamp                                    AS since,
       date_diff('minute', s.status_timestamp, now())        AS minutes,
       s.latitude, s.longitude
FROM sensors AS s
LEFT JOIN streets AS t USING (kerbsideid)
LEFT JOIN zones AS z USING (zone_number)

spec.label: Pedestrian counts (one row per counter and hour)
spec.name: peds

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: every pedestrian counter's hourly count over the time range,
-- through the gateway (see gateway/feeds.conf). The city loads the counts
-- once a day, so the latest hours are a day or two old. Whole days in
-- Melbourne, at most the last 31, so one URL stands for a day and the cache
-- can answer it. (A table function takes no subquery, so the dates are
-- written out in place.) A row's time is the start of its hour; day and hour
-- are Melbourne's. dir_1 and dir_2 are the two ways past the counter, named by
-- way_1 and way_2.
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT * FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/pedestrian-counting-system-monthly-counts-per-hour.parquet?select=location_id,sensing_date,hourday,direction_1,direction_2,pedestriancount&where=sensing_date%3E%3D%22'
                             || strftime(greatest(timezone('Australia/Melbourne', make_timestamptz(CAST(${__from} AS BIGINT) * 1000)), timezone('Australia/Melbourne', make_timestamptz(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000)) - INTERVAL 31 DAY), '%Y-%m-%d')
                             || '%22%20and%20sensing_date%3C%3D%22' || strftime(timezone('Australia/Melbourne', make_timestamptz(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000)), '%Y-%m-%d') || '%22')
),
places AS (
  SELECT location_id, sensor_description, direction_1 AS way_1, direction_2 AS way_2, latitude, longitude
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/pedestrian-counting-system-sensor-locations.parquet')
)
SELECT c.location_id::VARCHAR                                                   AS sensor,
       coalesce(p.sensor_description, 'Sensor ' || c.location_id)            AS name,
       timezone('Australia/Melbourne', c.sensing_date + to_hours(c.hourday))  AS time,
       strftime(c.sensing_date, '%Y-%m-%d')                                   AS day,
       c.hourday                                                              AS hour,
       c.pedestriancount                                                      AS people,
       c.direction_1 AS dir_1, c.direction_2 AS dir_2, p.way_1, p.way_2,
       p.latitude, p.longitude
FROM counts AS c LEFT JOIN places AS p USING (location_id)
WHERE p.latitude IS NOT NULL

-- Server side: the readings of the city's microclimate stations over the time
-- range, at most its last 14 days, through the gateway (see gateway/feeds.conf).
-- A station reports every 15 minutes or so; some have gone quiet, and only
-- those reporting in the range show up. Whole hours, so one URL stands for an
-- hour. The Royal Park weather station measures no noise or particles.
SELECT device_id                                   AS station,
       sensorlocation                              AS place,
       received_at                                 AS time,
       airtemperature                              AS temperature,
       relativehumidity                            AS humidity,
       averagewindspeed                            AS wind,
       gustwindspeed                               AS gust,
       pm25, pm10, noise,
       ST_Y(latlong) AS latitude, ST_X(latlong) AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/microclimate-sensors-data.parquet?where=received_at%3E%3D%22'
                  || strftime(greatest(date_trunc('hour', make_timestamp(CAST(${__from} AS BIGINT) * 1000)),
                                       date_trunc('hour', make_timestamp(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000)) - INTERVAL 14 DAY), '%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z')
                  || '%22%20and%20received_at%3C%22'
                  || strftime(date_trunc('hour', make_timestamp(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000)) + INTERVAL 1 HOUR, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z') || '%22')
